readmeExcerpt:
Flint: A Visualization Language for the AI Era

[**Project site**](https://microsoft.github.io/flint-chart/) · [**中文主页**](https://microsoft.github.io/flint-chart/#/zh) · [**MCP server**](https://microsoft.github.io/flint-chart/#/mcp)

Flint is a visualization language that lets **AI agents reliably create expressive, good-looking and interactive charts from simple, human-editable chart specs**. It is available as an [MCP server](https://microsoft.github.io/flint-chart/#/mcp) for everyday use with your agent, and as an [npm library](https://www.npmjs.com/package/flint-chart) for building interactive applications. Flint supports **52 chart types across 5 rendering backends** — [Vega-Lite](https://vega.github.io/vega-lite/), [ECharts](https://echarts.apache.org/), [Chart.js](https://www.chartjs.org/), [Plotly](https://plotly.com/javascript/), and native Excel charts — through one unified interface, with **14 themes and 23 interaction presets**. To create bespoke visualizations, design custom themes in the [Theme Lab](https://microsoft.github.io/flint-chart/#/theme-lab) and build [advanced interactions](https://microsoft.github.io/flint-chart/#/interactions/advanced) with the Flint API. https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c1cda0fa-3ea7-41af-b3fd-a127bc83d641

🔊 Click the speaker icon for sound  

## Updates - **October 19, 2026** — Flint 1.0 introduces [Flint Interactive](https://microsoft.github.io/flint-chart/#/interactions): interaction presets, semantic events, and an interaction API that connects charts to your app. ([changelog](CHANGELOG.md)) - **August 12, 2026** — Flint 0.5.1 extends visual themes to the Plotly backend and adds Vega-Lite Calendar Heatmap. - **August 5, 2026** — Flint 0.5.0 introduces formal visual themes with preset themes, custom ThemeSpec authoring, and preset inheritance. ([v0.5.0](https://github.com/microsoft/flint-chart/releases/tag/0.5.0)) - **July 24, 2026** — Flint 0.4.0 adds 38 Plotly chart types and 18 native, editable Excel chart templates. ([v0.4.0](https://github.com/microsoft/flint-chart/releases/tag/0.4.0)) See the [changelog](CHANGELOG.md) for every release. ## Get started ### In your agent app (MCP server) Chart right in the conversation with any MCP client, such as [GitHub Copilot in VS Code](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/copilot/chat/mcp-servers), [Claude](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/11175166-get-started-with-custom-connectors-using-remote-mcp), Claude Code, Codex, or Cursor. ⚡ **Quick start:** paste this setup request into your agent and let it configure Flint for the current project. For manual setup, see the [MCP server guide](https://microsoft.github.io/flint-chart/#/mcp). ```text Help me set up Flint as an MCP server named "flint"! 1. Add it to my client config, using whichever option my client supports: - a local (stdio) server: npx -y flint-chart-mcp - the hosted server over HTTP: https://flint.data-formulator.ai/mcp 2. Verify the setup by listing the available Flint chart types. 3. Show me a fun first chart: how many moons each planet has, in a Flint theme you like. ``` Then ask your agent for a chart, for example: ```text Go to Yahoo Finance, find today's percentage change for the Magnificent Seven tech stocks, and compare their performance with Flint in Economist style. Let me hover to read each stock's change. ``` The agent can open an interactive chart right in the conversation, return a static PNG or SVG, or produce a backend-native spec.

### Build with your coding agent Are you a developer building agent apps? Use [`flint-chart`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/flint-chart), Flint's npm library, to bring charts into your apps, dashboards, and data stories: ```bash npm install flint-chart ``` The library compiles Flint specs into backend-native chart specs and provides React and vanilla JavaScript APIs for embedding interactive charts. A Flint spec describes the data, semantic types, and field mappings, with optional theme and interaction settings. In React, pass it to `` to embed an interactive chart: ```tsx import type { ChartAssemblyInput } from 'flint-chart'; import { FlintChart } from 'flint-chart/react'; const spec: ChartAssemblyInput = { data: { values: [ { Month: '2026-01', Users: 1200 }, { Month: '2026-02', Users: 1800 }, ] }, semantic_types: { Month: 'YearMonth', Users: 'Quantity' }, chart_spec: { chartType: 'Line Chart', encodings: { x: 'Month', y: 'Users' }, }, theme_spec: 'economist', interaction_spec: { interactions: [{ type: 'inspect-index' }] }, }; ``` You can copy the following instruction to your coding agent to build a chart with Flint, then adapt it to your data and app: ```text Read Flint's chart authoring and interaction skills: https://github.com/microsoft/flint-chart/blob/main/agent-skills/flint-chart-author/SKILL.md https://github.com/microsoft/flint-chart/blob/main/agent-skills/flint-interaction-author/SKILL.md Use these skills to add a chart to this app. Install flint-chart and the renderer dependencies needed for this project. Plot monthly users by region from our data in Economist style. Let readers hover to compare regions at each month, and add a region selector that updates the chart. Integrate it with the app's existing layout and verify it works. ``` The agent can also generate backend-native specs or editable Excel charts for reports and documents. See the [API reference](docs/api-reference.md), [interaction API](docs/interaction-api.md), and [live editor](https://microsoft.github.io/flint-chart/#/editor) for the underlying APIs and examples. ## How it works A Flint spec consists of the data, semantic types, the chart spec, and optional theme and interaction specs. Instead of relying on complex user-side logic to glue them together, the compiler resolves each part against the others and composes a complete backend-native spec. ### 1. Describe data with semantic types Fields are described with semantic types such as `Rank`, `YearMonth`, `Delta`, or `Temperature`, along with their domains and units. The compiler uses them to infer parsing, scales, axes, formatting, and colors — a short Flint spec becomes a complete backend spec.

### 2. Build charts once, render on any backend Charts are defined with high-level chart types and encodings. The compiler adapts sizing, spacing, labels, and legends to the data, for example as it gets denser, and the same spec renders across Vega-Lite, ECharts, Chart.js, and Plotly, or as native Excel charts. See the [API reference](docs/api-reference.md) and the [gallery](https://microsoft.github.io/flint-chart/#/gallery). ### 3. Unify the look with a theme spec Geometry, typography, and color are reusable formal specs that apply across a whole chart library, independent of the data and chart type. Pick one of 14 preset themes, such as the New York Times, the Economist, Swiss, or McKinsey, or inherit one and override only what belongs to your brand: ```ts theme_spec: { extends: 'economist', id: 'our-brand', ink: { series: { single: '#6b3fa0' } } } ``` Compare every preset in the [theme explorer](https://microsoft.github.io/flint-chart/#/themes), design your own in the [Theme Lab](https://microsoft.github.io/flint-chart/#/theme-lab), and see the [theme guide](docs/theme-spec.md) for the full reference.

### 4. Add interactions with an interaction spec Flint provides 23 interaction presets and a programming API for building interactive charts into applications. The compiler resolves user interaction events into semantic information, so your app only answers with high-level chart updates: ```tsx import { FlintChart } from 'flint-chart/react'; { if (phase === 'commit') table.filter(state.selected); }} /> ```

Try the presets in the [interaction gallery](https://microsoft.github.io/flint-chart/#/interactions/gallery), see bespoke ones in [advanced interactions](https://microsoft.github.io/flint-chart/#/interactions/advanced), and read the [interaction spec](docs/interaction-spec.md) and [programming API](docs/interaction-api.md). ## Documentation - [Project site](https://microsoft.github.io/flint-chart/) — gallery, live editor, themes, and interactions - [API reference](docs/api-reference.md) and backend references for [Vega-Lite](docs/reference-vegalite.md), [ECharts](docs/reference-echarts.md), [Chart.js](docs/reference-chartjs.md), [Plotly](docs/reference-plotly.md), and [Excel](docs/reference-excel.md) - [Theme guide](docs/theme-spec.md), [interaction spec](docs/interaction-spec.md), and [interaction programming API](docs/interaction-api.md) - [MCP server guide](https://microsoft.github.io/flint-chart/#/mcp) and [agent skills](agent-skills/) - [Paper on arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20775) A Python port is in preview as source in [`packages/flint-py`](packages/flint-py); its package is not yet released. ## Contributing Contributions are welcome — especially new [chart templates](docs/adding-a-chart-template.md) and [rendering backends](docs/adding-a-backend.md). See [CONTRIBUTING](.github/CONTRIBUTING.md) and the [development guide](docs/DEVELOPMENT.md). ```bash git clone https://github.com/microsoft/flint-chart cd flint-chart npm install # workspaces: packages/flint-js, packages/flint-mcp, site npm run typecheck # typecheck flint-chart and flint-chart-mcp npm run test # Vitest for both packages npm run build # build both packages npm run site # project site, gallery, and editor at http://localhost:5274/ ``` Node 18+ is required. The site aliases `flint-chart` to `packages/flint-js/src`, so library edits hot-reload without rebuilding.

readmeHtml:
Flint: A Visualization Language for the AI Era

Project site · 中文主页 · MCP server

Flint is a visualization language that lets AI agents reliably create expressive, good-looking and interactive charts from simple, human-editable chart specs. It is available as an MCP server for everyday use with your agent, and as an npm library for building interactive applications.

Flint supports 52 chart types across 5 rendering backends — Vega-Lite, ECharts, Chart.js, Plotly, and native Excel charts — through one unified interface, with 14 themes and 23 interaction presets. To create bespoke visualizations, design custom themes in the Theme Lab and build advanced interactions with the Flint API.

flint-interactive-EN-white-web.mp4

🔊 Click the speaker icon for sound  

Updates

  • October 19, 2026 — Flint 1.0 introduces Flint Interactive: interaction presets, semantic events, and an interaction API that connects charts to your app. (changelog)
  • August 12, 2026 — Flint 0.5.1 extends visual themes to the Plotly backend and adds Vega-Lite Calendar Heatmap.
  • August 5, 2026 — Flint 0.5.0 introduces formal visual themes with preset themes, custom ThemeSpec authoring, and preset inheritance. (v0.5.0)
  • July 24, 2026 — Flint 0.4.0 adds 38 Plotly chart types and 18 native, editable Excel chart templates. (v0.4.0)

See the changelog for every release.

Get started

In your agent app (MCP server)

Chart right in the conversation with any MCP client, such as GitHub Copilot in VS Code, Claude, Claude Code, Codex, or Cursor.

⚡ Quick start: paste this setup request into your agent and let it configure Flint for the current project. For manual setup, see the MCP server guide.

Help me set up Flint as an MCP server named "flint"!

1. Add it to my client config, using whichever option my client supports:
   - a local (stdio) server: npx -y flint-chart-mcp
   - the hosted server over HTTP: https://flint.data-formulator.ai/mcp
2. Verify the setup by listing the available Flint chart types.
3. Show me a fun first chart: how many moons each planet has, in a Flint theme you like.

Then ask your agent for a chart, for example:

Go to Yahoo Finance, find today's percentage change for the Magnificent Seven
tech stocks, and compare their performance with Flint in Economist style.
Let me hover to read each stock's change.

The agent can open an interactive chart right in the conversation, return a static PNG or SVG, or produce a backend-native spec.

Build with your coding agent

Are you a developer building agent apps? Use flint-chart, Flint's npm library, to bring charts into your apps, dashboards, and data stories:

npm install flint-chart

The library compiles Flint specs into backend-native chart specs and provides React and vanilla JavaScript APIs for embedding interactive charts.

A Flint spec describes the data, semantic types, and field mappings, with optional theme and interaction settings. In React, pass it to <FlintChart> to embed an interactive chart:

import type { ChartAssemblyInput } from 'flint-chart';
import { FlintChart } from 'flint-chart/react';

const spec: ChartAssemblyInput = {
  data: { values: [
    { Month: '2026-01', Users: 1200 },
    { Month: '2026-02', Users: 1800 },
  ] },
  semantic_types: { Month: 'YearMonth', Users: 'Quantity' },
  chart_spec: {
    chartType: 'Line Chart',
    encodings: { x: 'Month', y: 'Users' },
  },
  theme_spec: 'economist',
  interaction_spec: { interactions: [{ type: 'inspect-index' }] },
};

<FlintChart spec={spec} />

You can copy the following instruction to your coding agent to build a chart with Flint, then adapt it to your data and app:

Read Flint's chart authoring and interaction skills:
https://github.com/microsoft/flint-chart/blob/main/agent-skills/flint-chart-author/SKILL.md
https://github.com/microsoft/flint-chart/blob/main/agent-skills/flint-interaction-author/SKILL.md

Use these skills to add a chart to this app.
Install flint-chart and the renderer dependencies needed for this project.
Plot monthly users by region from our data in Economist style.
Let readers hover to compare regions at each month, and add a region selector
that updates the chart.
Integrate it with the app's existing layout and verify it works.

The agent can also generate backend-native specs or editable Excel charts for reports and documents. See the API reference, interaction API, and live editor for the underlying APIs and examples.

How it works

A Flint spec consists of the data, semantic types, the chart spec, and optional theme and interaction specs. Instead of relying on complex user-side logic to glue them together, the compiler resolves each part against the others and composes a complete backend-native spec.

1. Describe data with semantic types

Fields are described with semantic types such as Rank, YearMonth, Delta, or Temperature, along with their domains and units. The compiler uses them to infer parsing, scales, axes, formatting, and colors — a short Flint spec becomes a complete backend spec.

2. Build charts once, render on any backend

Charts are defined with high-level chart types and encodings. The compiler adapts sizing, spacing, labels, and legends to the data, for example as it gets denser, and the same spec renders across Vega-Lite, ECharts, Chart.js, and Plotly, or as native Excel charts. See the API reference and the gallery.

3. Unify the look with a theme spec

Geometry, typography, and color are reusable formal specs that apply across a whole chart library, independent of the data and chart type. Pick one of 14 preset themes, such as the New York Times, the Economist, Swiss, or McKinsey, or inherit one and override only what belongs to your brand:

theme_spec: { extends: 'economist', id: 'our-brand', ink: { series: { single: '#6b3fa0' } } }

Compare every preset in the theme explorer, design your own in the Theme Lab, and see the theme guide for the full reference.

4. Add interactions with an interaction spec

Flint provides 23 interaction presets and a programming API for building interactive charts into applications. The compiler resolves user interaction events into semantic information, so your app only answers with high-level chart updates:

import { FlintChart } from 'flint-chart/react';

<FlintChart
  spec={{ ...input, interaction_spec: { interactions: [{ type: 'brush-x' }] } }}
  onChange={({ phase, state }) => {
    if (phase === 'commit') table.filter(state.selected);
  }}
/>

Try the presets in the interaction gallery, see bespoke ones in advanced interactions, and read the interaction spec and programming API.

Documentation

  • Project site — gallery, live editor, themes, and interactions
  • API reference and backend references for Vega-Lite, ECharts, Chart.js, Plotly, and Excel
  • Theme guide, interaction spec, and interaction programming API
  • MCP server guide and agent skills
  • Paper on arXiv

A Python port is in preview as source in packages/flint-py; its package is not yet released.

Contributing

Contributions are welcome — especially new chart templates and rendering backends. See CONTRIBUTING and the development guide.

git clone https://github.com/microsoft/flint-chart
cd flint-chart
npm install         # workspaces: packages/flint-js, packages/flint-mcp, site

npm run typecheck   # typecheck flint-chart and flint-chart-mcp
npm run test        # Vitest for both packages
npm run build       # build both packages
npm run site        # project site, gallery, and editor at http://localhost:5274/

Node 18+ is required. The site aliases flint-chart to packages/flint-js/src, so library edits hot-reload without rebuilding.

Repository layout 
flint-chart/
├── packages/
│   ├── flint-js/       npm package `flint-chart` (TypeScript)
│   │   └── src/
│   │       ├── core/         semantics, themes, layout, decisions, shared types
│   │       ├── chart-types/  shared chart definitions and template metadata
│   │       ├── interactive/  interaction presets and runtime
│   │       ├── react/        the `<FlintChart>` React component
│   │       ├── vegalite/     Vega-Lite backend
│   │       ├── echarts/      ECharts backend
│   │       ├── chartjs/      Chart.js backend
│   │       ├── plotly/       Plotly backend
│   │       ├── excel/        native Excel backend
│   │       └── test-data/    fixtures and stress-test generators
│   ├── flint-mcp/      MCP server `flint-chart-mcp`, MCP App UI, and tests
│   └── flint-py/       Python port preview
├── site/               Vite + React project site, gallery, editor, and docs
├── agent-skills/       chart, theme, and interaction authoring skills for agents
├── docs/               user, API, backend, and architecture documentation
└── design-docs/        design proposals and implementation research

This project has adopted the Microsoft Open Source Code of Conduct. See SECURITY.md to report vulnerabilities.

Community

Join the Flint Discord
Ask questions, share your charts, and follow releases with Flint users everywhere.

Join Discord 		Join the Flint WeChat group
Scan the QR code to join the Flint user WeChat group.

Contributors

We'd love to have you join us! Pick up an issue, add a chart template or a theme, or share what you build in the community. See Contributing to get started, and everyone on the contributors graph.

releases.name: Flint 1.0: Interactivity
releases.body: ## Flint 1.0: the language for interactive data visualizations In this release, Flint makes interactions easy to specify: from linked brushing and annotations to semantic zoom and coordinated chart–table views. Start with ready-made presets or build custom behaviors using data-level events and update operators. You describe the interaction; Flint handles the low-level wiring. Interaction support is now available in both the [MCP server](https://microsoft.github.io/flint-chart/#/mcp) and the [npm library](https://www.npmjs.com/package/flint-chart)! Explore the [interaction presets](https://microsoft.github.io/flint-chart/#/interactions/gallery), try the [custom interaction demos](https://microsoft.github.io/flint-chart/#/interactions/advanced), or dive into the [interaction API](https://microsoft.github.io/flint-chart/#/documentation/interaction-api) to build your own. Watch the video below to learn more. :) https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/23b1fa91-ed7a-4c1f-8211-25c058d8aad6 ## Examples

## flint-chart 0.5.1

**Added**

- **Plotly theme support** — `theme_spec` now realizes onto Plotly figures.
- **Calendar Heatmap** chart type for Vega-Lite.

**Titles**

- Headlines *and* decks are fitted instead of widening the graphic, with or without a theme.
- Axis titles lie flat at the head of their own ruler; units are stated once.

**Grid and scales**

- Gridded axes round so the plot edge lands on a grid line, and the grid runs out to its number.
- A chart is never left with no way to read a value — where nothing is printed, the grid returns.

**Houses** — Economist type recalibrated; McKinsey's tick labels no longer outrank its subtitle.

**Security** — react-router CSRF and two other high-severity dev alerts resolved; production audit clean.

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/microsoft/flint-chart/compare/0.5...0.5.1
New contributor: @zl190

releases.name: Flint 0.5: ThemeSpec
releases.body:
Flint 0.5 introduces `ThemeSpec`, a formal specification for applying a coherent design system across an entire chart library. Instead of requiring creators or agents to reproduce design guidance chart by chart, a ThemeSpec participates directly in compilation and adapts to the chart's semantics, data, cardinality, and available space. A ThemeSpec shapes compilation in three stages. Using resolved semantic information, it: - governs layout constraints and dynamics, including density, spacing, sizing, and stretch limits; - conditionally resolves visual preferences for labels, legends, axes, annotations, and semantic roles; and - supplies design fixtures such as typography, color, surfaces, mark geometry, and structural line styles to backend-specific code generation.

releases.body: Flint 0.3 makes charts easier to explore after they are created. The MCP App can now switch chart types and edit chart properties in place, while the original Flint spec stays compact and readable. ### Explore chart types Move between compatible views without rebuilding the chart. For example, turn a dense Line Chart of food prices into compact Sparkline rows for easier comparison. Flint preserves the data roles and derives the details for the new chart type. ### Edit chart properties Edit common properties directly in the widget. aiSummary.oneLiner: A visualization intermediate language that lets AI agents create expressive charts from simple specs.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: Flint is a visualization language designed specifically for the AI era. It acts as an intermediate layer, allowing AI agents to generate polished, expressive charts from human-readable specifications. It simplifies the process of creating complex data visualizations by bridging the gap between raw data and visual output. It provides a structured format that both LLMs and humans can understand and modify. This enables seamless integration of data visualization capabilities into various AI-driven applications and workflows. The language abstracts away pixel-level rendering logic into high-level declarative design tokens.
keyFeatures: AI-native format: Designed to be easily generated and parsed by large language models.
Human-editable specs: Uses a simple specification format that developers can easily read and modify.
Polished visual output: Renders high-quality, expressive charts from the intermediate representation.
MCP Server support: Includes integration guides for Model Context Protocol servers.
Cross-platform design: Aims to be a universal intermediate language for data visualization tasks.
